title: The Legend of Zelda Movie Reveals Its Official Logo — and Nintendo Confirms There’s No Subtitle
description: Nintendo has revealed the official logo for its live-action The Legend of Zelda movie and confirmed that the April 2027 film will simply be titled The Legend of Zelda.
body:
Nintendo has revealed the official logo for its upcoming live-action **The Legend of Zelda** movie during the series’ 40th Anniversary Direct.

The company also confirmed one deceptively important detail about the film’s identity: **there is no subtitle**. Nintendo’s first live-action Zelda movie is simply called *The Legend of Zelda*.

The reveal does not give us the full trailer fans are still waiting for, but it does settle the branding of a project that is due to bring Hyrule to theaters on **April 30, 2027**.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: The official The Legend of Zelda live-action movie logo shown during Nintendo’s Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, with the film’s April 30, 2027 theatrical release date.
imageCredit: Nintendo / The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct

contentBlocks.text: During The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, Nintendo showed the movie’s official logo and confirmed that the film will use **The Legend of Zelda** as its complete title. There is no extra subtitle attached. That may sound like a small detail, but it establishes how Nintendo wants to present its first live-action Zelda adaptation: as the theatrical version of the franchise itself rather than a film named after one specific game or adventure.
contentBlocks.heading: What Nintendo actually revealed

contentBlocks.text: **Benjamin Evan Ainsworth** is set to play Link, while **Bo Bragason** will portray Princess Zelda. The film is being directed by **Wes Ball**, whose recent credits include *Kingdom of the Planet of the Apes*. Nintendo veteran **Shigeru Miyamoto** is producing alongside **Avi Arad**. The anniversary presentation did not replace those earlier announcements; today’s update was focused on the movie’s final title treatment and branding.
contentBlocks.heading: The Zelda movie already has its Link and Zelda

contentBlocks.text: The live-action **The Legend of Zelda** movie is currently scheduled to open worldwide on **April 30, 2027**. That gives Nintendo plenty of time to reveal the film itself in greater detail, including the first substantial trailer, its version of Hyrule and which parts of the games will shape the story.
contentBlocks.heading: When does The Legend of Zelda movie release?

contentBlocks.text: Nintendo could have tied the film directly to a recognizable game such as *Ocarina of Time*, *Breath of the Wild* or *Twilight Princess*. Instead, calling it simply *The Legend of Zelda* suggests the company wants the movie to stand as an entry point to the entire series. The logo reveal is therefore useful confirmation for anyone trying to understand whether this is being marketed as an adaptation of one particular Zelda game or as a broader cinematic take on the franchise.
contentBlocks.heading: Why the lack of a subtitle matters

conclusion: The 40th Anniversary Direct did not deliver the full Zelda movie trailer, but Nintendo has now locked in something fundamental: the film’s public identity. It is **The Legend of Zelda**, without a subtitle, and the next major question is no longer what Nintendo will call it — it is when we will finally see Hyrule in motion.
